root_causes.evidence: The reconciliation session held a ledger write lock (UPDATE accounts, about 13 s). Payments logged repeated 'database is locked' failures, and ledger write_errors went to 0 after release_lock.
Clearing was down (exit code 15, no error logs) with 44 items queued and the head item at 0 attempts. After a restart it drained the queue to the network with no errors.

Payments 1.5 was deployed just before the symptoms. After the lock was gone it still failed about 58% with p95 around 1.2 s ('response could not be completed') and duplicate payments kept rising. Rolling back to 1.3 brought errors to 0, p95 to 46 ms, and stopped the duplicates at 143.

actions.reason: Payments failures are 'database is locked' caused by the reconciliation session holding a ledger write lock; release it first.
Clearing exited with code 15 (terminated) and logged no errors or poison item, so this looks like process_down; restart it.

Lock errors stopped after the release, but payments 1.5 (deployed just before the symptoms) still fails ~58% with slow 'response could not be completed' and rising duplicate payments, so roll it back.

escalation.reason: All components are back at baseline and the probe passes, but release 1.5 left 143 duplicate payments in the ledger. I cannot reverse or refund money, so I will hand that over to a person before closing.; past damage, no longer growing: data check failed: duplicate payments = 143
escalation.to: the on-call engineer; the operations team
escalation.ask: Payments release 1.5 (deployed by ops-maintenance) created 143 duplicate payments before it was rolled back to 1.3. The count has stayed at 143 since the rollback. Many of these were likely cleared to the network. Please identify the duplicate payments in the ledger and remediate them with the network and affected customers through the normal reversal process; the incident commander may not move or reverse money. Also please fix release 1.5 before it is redeployed. Separately, the reconciliation batch held a ledger write lock long enough to block payments. That session was ended and its transaction rolled back, so please rerun reconciliation and review how it locks the ledger.; find and put right the records behind 'data check failed: duplicate payments = 143'; the incident commander cannot change data

sbar.situation: The bank system has recovered and is back at baseline. The payment probe passes end to end, and the last of three recovery checks, at 74 s, was clean (2 of 2 in a row).
sbar.background: Payments release 1.5 was deployed by ops-maintenance just before the symptoms began. At the same time, the reconciliation session held a ledger write lock (UPDATE accounts, about 13 s), and clearing was down with exit code 15 and 44 items queued.
sbar.assessment: The incident commander took three actions itself. It ended the reconciliation session holding the ledger lock, which brought ledger write errors to 0; it restarted clearing, which drained the queue to the network with no errors; and it rolled payments back from 1.5 to 1.3, which brought errors to 0, cut p95 from about 1.2 s to 46 ms, and stopped duplicate payments at 143.
sbar.recommendation: The operations team must find the 143 duplicate payments in the ledger and reverse them with the network and affected customers through the normal reversal process, as many were likely cleared. The incident commander cannot move money or change data. Fix payments release 1.5 before redeploying it, and rerun reconciliation (its transaction was rolled back) and review how it locks the ledger.
